answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may place orders. When identities coordinate to manipulate prices or claim rewards, the protocol can slash deposits tied to provable violations, so creating a swarm multiplies the capital at risk instead of multiplying influence for free. The rule applies equally on an island market, in a sable-trading exchange, or across a karst network; the attacker pays upfront and risks losing funds for each identity caught cheating.
